knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given Its Graph

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124473/plots/plot-ea76c21f2622146ad8f65790adffa3ff5116d4b419de97d044f33f5fc58d6a42.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

Select all that apply.

I. $x\in (-2,0]$

II. $x\in [0,2]$

III. $x\in [-1,2]$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- On interval I, $x\in (-2,0]$, the function is invertible. Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the restricted graph at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

- On interval II, $x\in [0,2]$, the function is invertible. Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the restricted graph at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

- On interval III, $x\in [-1,2]$, the function is **not** invertible. Some horizontal lines will intersect the restricted graph more than once.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
